newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen rising on high-tech optimism.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen rising on high-tech optimism.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to gain ground on Monday, as high-technology shares are expected to remain upbeat, helped by gains in computer shares in New York, brokers said.

But they added that any rise in the key stock index in Tokyo could be limited due to a possible sell-off in shares of some financially weak firms in the construction and retail sectors. The shares fell steeply last week.
On Friday, the 225-share Nikkei average gained 120.71 points or 0.61 percent to close at 19,875.49. Its September Nikkei futures rose 60 points to 19,840.

"As U.S. stocks closed higher and the yen has stabilised near 114.00 yen to the dollar, I expect the Nikkei 225 to keep a firm tone today," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities Co Ltd. He added that the index was likely to test 20,000 sometime this week.
On Friday, Wall Street stocks staged a broad rally that was paced by large gains in the computer sector, with the Dow industrials climbing 35.6 points to 7,921.82.
However, worries over some Japanese firms' financial problems are likely to keep weighing down their shares and limit gains in the Nikkei index.
These concerns have grown since general contractor Tokai Kogyo Co Ltd filed for court protection from creditors earlier this month.
"We don't know how much the Nikkei 225 can rise today as trade has polarised into two directions (of bullish shares and weak shares) recently," said a broker at a major Japanese securities house.
